questions.q: What is a 'data subject' in the context of a data subject request?
options: The individual whose personal data is being processed
The system administrator who processes the request
The department responsible for data classification
A third-party vendor that stores personal data
questions.explain: The data subject is the individual the personal data is about — the person invoking one of their rights over that data.

questions.q: Which of these is the right to 'data portability'?
options: Receiving personal data in a structured, commonly-used, machine-readable format to move to another provider
The right to have personal data permanently deleted
The right to restrict all processing of personal data indefinitely
The right to object to any marketing communication
questions.explain: Portability specifically concerns receiving data in a transferable format, distinct from access, erasure, restriction, or objection.

questions.q: Why is identity verification the first step in fulfilling a data subject request?
options: Because handing over, correcting, or deleting someone's data without confirming the requester's identity turns the right into an attack vector
Because it is required only for erasure requests, not access requests
Because verification replaces the need to locate the data afterward
Because it is the final step after the data has already been compiled
questions.explain: Skipping identity verification means an impersonator could successfully request another person's data or trigger deletion of someone else's records.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where does the DSR fulfillment process most often break down in practice?
options: Locating the data, because personal data is typically scattered across many systems including shadow IT
Logging the request, because logging is optional under most frameworks
Verifying identity, because most organizations have no verification process at all
Compiling the response, because export formats are universally standardized
questions.explain: Personal data is rarely confined to one system — it spreads across the application database, warehouse, CRM, support tools, logs, and sometimes unsanctioned spreadsheets, making it the hardest step to execute reliably.

questions.q: What does logging a data subject request accomplish, independent of the underlying personal data itself?
options: It creates a record of what was requested, when, and what was done, which demonstrates the obligation was honored
It automatically deletes the data once the response window closes
It replaces the need to verify the requester's identity
It classifies the data according to its sensitivity level
questions.explain: The log itself — not the data it concerns — is what lets an organization later prove it actually fulfilled its obligation to a specific request.
